title: Streamed KV cohort fusion experiments
body:
Purpose
Quick exploratory notes on an approach we prototyped for streaming paged-KV access that fuses small FlashAttention kernels with a lightweight cohort-based KV fetch pipeline. Goal: reduce per-token tail latency for long-context chat workloads while keeping memory pressure and kernel-launch overhead manageable.

Context and motivation
- Current paged-KV approach: page-in entire KV slabs into GPU DRAM, then run monolithic attention passes. Good throughput but suffers when many requests have long prefixes and small suffixes (chat turn workloads).
- Observed problem: tail latency dominated by repeated kernel launches and large-kernel setup cost when most tokens are local-cache hits but small amounts of new KV need loading.
- Hypothesis: If we stream KV pages in small cohorts and fuse their arrival with localized FlashAttention micro-kernels, we can:
  * Mask page load latency behind GPU compute,
  * Avoid large monolithic attention kernels for small suffixes,
  * Reduce per-request scheduler/launch overhead via cooperative batching of micro-requests.

Design sketch (cohort fusion):
- Cohort: a small group of concurrent requests that share recent context locality (e.g., same conversation or similar prefix hash). Cohorts formed at scheduler level (micro-cohort window ~8-32 requests).
- Streamed pipeline:
  1) Scheduler groups incoming requests into cohort buckets by prefix fingerprint.
  2) For each cohort, compute missing KV page set (diff) and enqueue asynchronous page loads (pinned host staging -> GPU staging).
  3) While pages stream in, launch small FlashAttention micro-kernels on the cohort's available KV slices to produce partial logits and warm KV caches. Micro-kernels operate on limited seq-l ranges (e.g., last 128 tokens).
  4) As remaining pages arrive, issue fusion-update micro-kernels that stitch new KV into partial attention outputs (incremental reduce).
  5) Finalize with a small consolidation pass that computes final logits for the cohort.
- Kernel-level idea: micro-kernels are FlashAttention variants specialized for short sequence lengths (<=128) and optimized for persistent register tiling and warp-level cooperation. Each micro-kernel is cheap to launch and yields partial outputs that are mergeable.

Kernel heuristics we tried
- Tile sizes: 32x32, 64x16, 16x64 (QxK blocks) — 64x16 had best occupancy on A100 for these shapes.
- Warp grouping: use 2 warps per Q tile to allow cooperative accumulate of KV contributions and reduce per-warp shared memory pressure.
- Persistent thread blocks: tried persistent TBs that loop over cohort members to amortize launch overhead. This reduced CPU->GPU launch stalls but increased register pressure.
- Use of tensor cores: micro-kernels convert attention matmuls to FP16/AMP paths for K and V loads. For small seq-l, tensor cores provide modest gains but need careful alignment to avoid fractional occupancy.

Experiment notes and microbench results (sanitised numbers)
- Baselines (monolithic attention pass): per-request P50=13.4ms, P95=46.1ms, GPU throughput for batch=16: 110 tokens/s.
- Micro-kernel cohort fused pipeline (cohort size 8, micro tile 64x16): P50=7.6ms, P95=22.9ms, throughput 135 tokens/s.
- Persistent TB variant: P50 slightly lower (7.1ms) but P95 similar; however saw increased jitter under bursty arrivals.
- Memory overhead: cohort metadata + staging areas ~1.4MB per cohort.
- Host->GPU copy overlap ratio improved from 0.32 to 0.61 (fraction of page load time overlapped by compute).
- Observations: biggest wins when miss ratio per request < 35% and average new-page count per request small (<= 3).

Prototype pseudocode (high level)
- Note: pseudocode intentionally informal, for implement sketching.

  scheduler_loop():
    while true:
      req = dequeue_incoming()
      fp = prefix_hash(req.prefix)
      cohort = find_or_make_cohort(fp, window_ms=20)
      cohort.push(req)
      if cohort.ready_to_dispatch():
        launch_cohort_pipeline(cohort)

  launch_cohort_pipeline(cohort):
    missing_pages = cohort.compute_missing_page_set()
    for p in missing_pages:
      async_page_load_gpu(p, on_complete=page_arrived_callback)
    // kick off micro-kernel compute using pages already resident
    launch_micro_flashattn(cohort, seq_window=last_128)
    // later, page_arrived_callback will launch fusion_update kernels

  page_arrived_callback(page, cohort):
    mark_page_ready(page)
    if cohort.can_run_fusion_update():
      launch_fusion_update_kernel(cohort, page)

Fusion update kernels are designed to accept partial state and delta-KV and perform an incremental attention reduce.

Implementation details worth noting
- Cohort lifecycle: short-lived (~50–200ms), must be GC-cleaned quickly to avoid metadata heap growth.
- Backpressure: when page server bandwidth is saturated, throttle cohort formation window and fall back to monolithic path for strict-latency requests.
- Error handling: if a page fault cannot be resolved in-time, run fallback attention that treats missing KV as zero (best-effort partial answer) and send a degraded-quality response rather than blocking. This keeps p99 SLOs stable.
- Metrics to add: per-cohort miss_ratio, average pages_per_request, overlap_fraction, microkernel_launchs_per_request, fallback_rate.

Micro-optimizations tested (notes)
- Warp-level prefetch hints: inlined prefetch for next KV slice inside kernel reduced L2 thrash.
- Inline compression: Zstd-accelerated unpack on CPU pinned buffer then memcpy to GPU; tradeoff: CPU unpack latency dominates for tiny pages, but amortized for cohorts.
- Small-page coalescing: coalesce several tiny page loads into single larger DMA when they target contiguous GPU addresses; reduced PCIe transfer overhead by ~12%.
- Avoided atomic-heavy merge: used per-warp accumulation followed by single warp-store to reduce contention on partial-output buffers.

Failure modes and edge cases
- Large prefix divergence: when cohort members diverge quickly (branching conversation), micro-kernel wasted compute because partial outputs were not reusable. Mitigation: detect divergence and abort cohort fusion early to avoid wasted work.
- Memory fragmentation from staging buffers under high churn. Solution: pooled fixed-size staging buffers and recycler thread.
- Precision drift: incremental fusion updates had small fp16 accumulate errors vs monolithic float32 reference. Add occasional consolidation pass (fp32) for long-lived sequences, or run final consolidate in fp32 when QoE metric degrades.

Open questions / tradeoffs
- Cohort sizing policy: static (N=8) worked well in tests, but dynamic sizing by request arrival rate + miss_ratio might adapt better. Need policy experiments with live traffic.
- How to generalize fusion-update kernels to support cross-attention (encoder-decoder) paths — pattern is similar but KV layouts differ.
- Integration with rollout/AB testing: instrument cohort path and slowly route small % of production to measure real-world regressions.

Next steps / TODOs
- Clean up prototype code and move micro-kernels to runtime/kernels/streamed_cohort/* (PR referenced above).
- Add unit microbench harness that can replay synthetic chat traces with configurable miss patterns.
- Implement dynamic cohort sizing heuristic and safe fallback gate.
- Add metric exporters and dashboard prototype: cohort_latency, cohort_miss_ratio, fallback_rate.
- Run small-scale canary on dedicated infra for 1 week and gather p95/p99 and user-level quality metrics.

Notes to self / rough reminders
- watch for CUDA kernel register spilling when persistent TBs loop many cohort members -> hurts occupancy more than launch overhead saved.
- tune L2 prefetch hints conservatively; too many prefetches increase L2 eviction and hurt other tenants.
- compare against simple caching policy: keep last-k pages pinned per conversation vs cohort streaming. Might be sufficient and simpler.

References / links we used
- internal: serving-runtime/paged-kv-spec.md (draft), flashattention upstream docs, kernel microbench harness repo.
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/842
- Linear: https://linear.app/INF/issue/RT-741/paged-kv-cohort-experiments

Questions for review
- Does the cohort concept map cleanly to our existing request-routing pieces? (cc: @Leah Chen for routing impacts)
- Are FP16 incremental updates acceptable given downstream evals? Need to run a quality regression test with 1000 prompt set.

End of notes.

-- Sofia
